findings: Native deferred lookup returns an existing requested slot unchanged; on creation it registers the requested slot and optional behaviour before binding. Failed binding retains both; no reflection is used in the reconstruction.
Replace skips identical concrete types. Otherwise it stores the new unit before scanning the first matching behaviour id. A plain replacement leaves an old behaviour entry intact.

RemoveLateUnits removes all late behaviours first, then scans slots ascending and calls OnRemove before clearing each slot. A callback failure retains the failing slot; callback replacements in the same slot are cleared.

LevelContext publishes Current before permanent constructors. Activate resets the published random manager seed, creates a new clock, and for a new level arranges win-fail then binds all published units. IsActive is set only after success; a previously active state is not proactively reset on failure.

Clear deactivates globally and resets the shared explosion identity before clearing a borrowed live array in slot order. Only gameExit removes late units. ManualUpdate has no LevelContext-local activation gate; the parent GameContext supplies that gate.

Required factories/providers are not installed as dummy managers in production. Concrete permanent/win-fail implementations, parent-context clock registration and full application/player session startup remain required.

Ordinary clock construction/current delta/scaling and multicast late transport now have separate native verification and actual prefab-host Unity regression. Full parent GameContext activation/deactivation ownership is still required.
